input: Create a chore reward chart just for myself

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing which chores are included determines the size and structure of the chart — a few daily habits vs. a full household task list requires a very different layout.
The entire motivational mechanic depends on what the rewards are — points, treats, experiences, purchases — which shapes how the tracking system is built.
Whether this is used digitally (phone/computer) or physically (paper/whiteboard) completely changes the format and tools needed.
The time cycle for resetting or reviewing the chart (daily, weekly, monthly) affects how milestones and rewards are structured.
Understanding what the user wants to get out of this — accountability, fun, habit-building — determines how strict or flexible the system should be.
The visual style and tone (playful/gamified vs. clean/minimal) shapes the design and whether it feels rewarding to engage with.
Knowing the very next action — whether to build a template, recommend an app, or draft a list of chores — determines where to start immediately.

gold.taskTitle: Build a personal chore reward chart
gold.taskDescription: Create a self-directed chore reward chart that tracks tasks and motivates the user through a personal reward system.

questions.title: Which specific chores do you want to track?
questions.description: Identify the exact chores to include — e.g., dishes, laundry, vacuuming — versus a broad or open-ended list, to define the chart's scope.

questions.title: What rewards will you give yourself for completing chores?
questions.description: Determine the reward mechanic — points toward a treat, screen time, a purchase, a fun activity — since this is the core motivational engine of the chart.

questions.title: Will this chart live on paper or on a device?
questions.description: Decide whether the chart will be physical (printed sheet, whiteboard) or digital (spreadsheet, app, notes), as this dictates the tools and format needed.

questions.title: How often should the chart reset — daily, weekly, or monthly?
questions.description: Establish the time cycle for tracking and resetting chore completion, which determines how milestones and reward thresholds are structured.

questions.title: What is the main goal — building habits, having fun, or accountability?
questions.description: Clarify the primary purpose driving this chart so the system can be calibrated to be as strict, flexible, or gamified as needed.

questions.title: Should the chart feel playful and gamified, or clean and minimal?
questions.description: Define the visual tone and style so the chart design feels personally motivating and enjoyable to interact with daily.

questions.title: Do you want a ready-to-use template or a custom built-from-scratch chart?
questions.description: Determine the immediate next action — finding an existing template to adapt, or building a bespoke chart from the ground up.
